name: Gemini 4 Carbon
archDisplay: Proprietary model; architecture and parameter count undisclosed; 1M-token context
note: Google DeepMind's Oct 28, 2026 frontier model, the successor to Gemini 4 Argon. Like Argon, it rolled out first to selected users (trusted cyber defenders in the Fairwind Program); on Nov 10, 2026 Google made it available on the paid tier of the Gemini API (AI Studio) and Gemini for business, and is rolling it out to AI Ultra. Introductory price is $2/$10 per Mtok until Nov 30, 2026, then $4/$20; following the Argon precedent the headline price is the introductory $2/$10 (Vals AI bills its runs at $4/$20). ctxK is 1000 from the 1M-token window Vals AI and Artificial Analysis list. Vals AI's independent runs put it #2 of 29 on the Vals Index (70.36), #1 of 87 on Legal Research Bench and #4 of 57 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (63.13). Artificial Analysis puts it #1 on Intelligence Index v5 (59) and reports Terminal-Bench 4.0 65.2% and Terminal-Bench-Science 64.8% on its own harness; Google's table quotes those AA figures. NOT FILED: the AA Terminal-Bench rows (the corpus columns use the Vals boards; Vals has no Terminal-Bench-Science run for Carbon yet); Agents' Last Exam v1.1 (77.4) and OSWorld-2.1 offline (81.5) are newer versions than the corpus columns; CWE-bench 71.0 is above the column's bounds (normMax 60, as with Argon's 68.0); Vals Finance Agent v2.1 (67.16) and HLAB-Vals-1.1 (17.50) are not comparable with the v2/v1 columns; SWE-sweep, GraphWalks, RiemannBench, Vending-Bench 2, Blueprint-Bench 2, ExploitGym, Vals Index and AA Index have no corpus column.
